content: There are no known interactions between dexlansoprazole and specific foods or beverages. However, it is unclear whether consuming alcohol has any effect on dexlansoprazole. Regarding drug interactions, it is essential to inform your healthcare provider about all prescription and over-the-counter (OTC) medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and other supplements you are currently using. Specifically, you should discuss the use of the following medications before starting dexlansoprazole: Methotrexate (e.g., Trexall and others) Digoxin (e.g., Lanoxin), which is used to treat irregular heartbeats and certain types of heart failure Warfarin, a blood thinner Tacrolimus, commonly used to prevent organ transplant rejection Certain antiretroviral medications, such as rilpivirine (Edurant), nelfinavir (Viracept), or saquinavir (Invirase), which are used for HIV or AIDS St. John’s Wort Rifampin (e.g., Rimactane and others), a medication used to treat tuberculosis (TB) Some medications may alter the blood levels of dexlansoprazole, and dexlansoprazole may, in turn, affect the absorption or effectiveness of other drugs. Therefore, it is crucial to inform your healthcare provider about all medications you are taking or have recently taken. This list may not include all possible drug interactions with dexlansoprazole. In the event of an overdose of dexlansoprazole, seek immediate medical attention by calling 911 or contacting a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. If you miss a dose of dexlansoprazole, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and proceed with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take double or extra doses to make up for a missed dose. Adding plans to your medication management system allows you to compare formulary status with other drugs in the same class.
